title: Language changes inside a page need valid codes
summary: A lang attribute on an element inside the page holds an invalid language code. Use a valid code such as fr so screen readers pronounce it correctly.
problem: An element inside the page has a lang attribute with a value that is not a valid language code, such as "french" instead of "fr". It is meant to mark a passage in another language.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users, whose software switches voice for marked passages. With an invalid code it keeps the page voice and reads the foreign phrase with the wrong pronunciation.
whyItMatters: A correct code lets speech software pronounce a phrase properly. This is a WCAG 3.1.2 failure at Level AA, the level that accessibility regulations and procurement requirements commonly build on.
steps: Find the element with the invalid lang value in the scan result.
Replace it with a valid BCP 47 code, such as fr, de or es-MX.
Mark only passages that are in a different language from the page. Names and borrowed words that are widely known do not need it.
Also fix any xml:lang attribute on the same element.
before: Our motto is joie de vivre, which means enjoying life.
after: Our motto is joie de vivre, which means enjoying life.
howToCheck: Search the page source for lang= and check each value. Every one should be a short code such as fr or es-MX, not a language name.
